source.title: Scaling Neural Machine Translation
source.authors: Myle Ott; Sergey Edunov; D. Grangier; M. Auli

record.tranche_reason: Compares validation loss across batch sizes by epochs, a direct but limited measure of large-batch held-out performance.
record.gate_note: Figure 1 reports validation-loss curves by optimization steps and epochs; the text explicitly describes slower initial convergence by epochs. Table 1 reports time to a target validation perplexity under progressively changed training setups, so it does not isolate batch size or measure a generalization gap.
record.test_reason: Figure 1 compares held-out translation loss at equal numbers of training epochs across batch sizes, extending V5's batch-size question to neural machine translation. The text explicitly reports an initial disadvantage for larger batches.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the batch-size discussion but incompletely summarizes the paper. The authors conclude that reduced precision, large batches and increased learning rates together accelerate big-Transformer training nearly fivefold on eight GPUs; distributed training delivers strong translation accuracy rapidly, although multi-node scaling retains substantial overhead.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates large-batch Transformer training for translation efficiency, not the generalization-gap measurements in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size and measurement axis (epochs versus optimization steps); learning-rate increase with large batches.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger batches converge faster per optimization step, and increasing the learning rate reduces wall-clock time to a target validation perplexity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large-batch translation training can improve update efficiency and training speed. These comparisons do not establish that an accuracy penalty disappears at a fixed epoch budget.

record.problems: Figure 1 provides curves without exact values in the supplied text. The paper does not report training error or a train-test gap; batch-size changes are combined with learning-rate changes in some efficiency comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible additional results. Table 1's time-to-validation-perplexity results change several training settings together and do not isolate the batch-size effect on held-out performance.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning budgets.

Image classification and language modeling; persistence of the penalty at later fixed epoch budgets; whether longer training or recipe changes remove it at matched epoch budgets. Learning-rate warmup and decay are indexed by updates, so equal epochs do not imply equal schedule positions.
Dropout ablations, including interactions with dataset size and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V5. Remove the record's limits_scope verdict: faster convergence per update or wall-clock minute does not qualify a claim explicitly conditioned on fixed epochs. A train–test gap is unnecessary for V5 because held-out performance itself is the named outcome. Table 1's efficiency comparisons were already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance.

The study tests batch-size effects on validation loss by epochs for WMT English-German translation. It does not report a training-test error gap, language-model results, or a fixed-epoch comparison across adaptive recipes.
Sharpness or other measured properties tracking the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

relationships.condition: Early fixed epoch budgets for the WMT En-De Transformer, comparing 100k–400k-token batches with 25k-token batches
relationships.reason: R2–R4, relative to R1, show the initial held-out-loss disadvantage described explicitly in Section 4.2; exact losses and a lasting penalty are not established.
relationships.display_finding: The study's results suggest higher held-out loss early in training with larger batches, without establishing exact losses or a lasting penalty. These results have not been verified.
